transcript.text: Zanussi dishwasher keeps tripping the electrics, not every time though. Usually about 15 mins in. Model ZDT21006FA

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. A dishwasher tripping the electrics is a safety issue. Because this involves live electrical parts and water, please do not keep trying to run it until we have identified the cause; repeated tripping can indicate a fault that may worsen. The fact that it usually trips about 15 minutes into the cycle gives us a strong clue. In most dishwashers, this timing coincides with the heating phase (when the water is being heated) or the main wash circulation. The two most likely causes are: 1. A failing heater element: Over time, the insulation inside the element can break down, causing it to 'leak' electricity to earth when hot. This often trips the RCD only once heating starts.
2. A fault in the circulation pump or its wiring: If the trip happens during the wash phase but before significant heating, it could be the motor or a wire rubbing against the casing. To narrow this down safely, I need to know exactly when the trip occurs:
• Does it happen the moment you turn the power on (before any water moves)?
• Does it happen once the machine starts filling and washing?
• Does it happen specifically when the heating stage begins (usually after 10-20 minutes)? Please let me know which of these matches your experience.

It doesn't trip when I switch it on. It's usually 10-20 mins into the 65C programme, so probably around when it heats. A quick cold rinse never trips it. It's happened 3 times in 2 weeks and no burning smell. The trip takes out the fridge too, which is on the same circuit, so I'm a bit worried.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
As the element heats up, any degradation in its insulation expands or conducts, causing the RCD (the trip that cuts power to your fridge too) to detect a fault and switch off. Because this is an electrical safety hazard involving water, you must not continue to run the dishwasher until it has been repaired by a qualified engineer. Repeated tripping can indicate worsening insulation failure, which could eventually lead to a more serious fault or damage other components on that circuit. 1. 2. You do not attempt to open the machine to test the element yourself unless you are qualified to work on live electrical systems and understand how to safely isolate and discharge capacitors.
3. You check that no water is pooling around the plug or socket, as this could also contribute to tripping, though it wouldn't explain the specific timing during the heating phase. The engineer will likely need to check the heater element (or the flow-through heater assembly if your model uses an integrated unit). Please arrange for a qualified appliance repair technician to inspect and fix this.
